title: SAP Document AI — What a Two-Invoice Evidence Handover Can Support
subtitle: Reported synthetic invoice extraction results, unreproduced field checks, and proposed Finance controls
evidence_status: Owner handover-reported results only; source-PDF/export field comparison not independently replayed for this publication
lineage_note: This public draft reflects a prior owner-supplied KS05 handover. Reported 34/34 field matches and 12 address-field anomalies were not re-established by an independent source-PDF-to-export replay in the R2 reviewer execution. No current SAP tenant/catalog read or Finance business-process test is established. Statements below distinguish reports from independently verified activity.

sections.title: Why evaluate SAP Document AI if OCR exists?
sections.markdown:
**Question: Why consider SAP Document AI when OCR already exists?**

**Direct answer:** OCR recognizes text; SAP Document AI is designed to extract structured **business document fields** such as invoice headers and line items through supported machine-learning or template-based methods, with reviewable extraction results and documented enrichment options. These may reduce bespoke parsing effort when an existing OCR system produces only text. Document AI can itself involve OCR; the architecture question is not whether text recognition is replaced.

**Do not adopt another service automatically.** If an existing OCR/IDP platform already produces accurate structured invoices, controlled exceptions and approved SAP integrations at a lower total cost, it may remain the better choice. Compare the alternatives on **field-level correctness, unsupported populated fields, human corrections, integration and operational cost per validated invoice**.

**What KS05 actually provides:** two synthetic supplier invoices described by an owner handover. The reported **34/34** selected-field matches and **12** address-field concerns were **not independently rechecked against the original PDFs/exports** for this publication. No current-tenant inventory, comparator OCR benchmark, supplier/PO validation or Finance posting was verified.

**Architectural lesson:** Extracting a value is not the same as proving it is supported by the document or authorized master data. Validation and approval remain separate gates.

sections.title: Two synthetic invoice documents
sections.markdown:
The KS05 handover describes two synthetic supplier-invoice PDFs and manually supplied extraction exports, with the same invented business identity and amounts. **The counts below are handover-reported, not independently reproduced for this publication candidate.** The reviewer did not obtain a reproducible source-PDF-to-export check and could not independently establish document-ID linkage.

| Handover item | Reported result / evidence status |
| --- | --- |
| Selected header-field matches | 9 per invoice, **reported, not replayed** |
| Selected line-field matches | 8 per invoice, **reported, not replayed** |
| Total selected field matches | **34/34 reported**, 17 per invoice; **unverified by fresh source replay** |
| Address-designated source-support issues | **12 reported**, six per invoice; **not independently rechecked** |
| Export-to-document-ID linkage | **Not established in the reviewed publication evidence** |
| Fresh tenant catalog and processing status | **Not verified** |
| SAP Finance duplicate rejection or posting | **No validation evidence supplied** |

The numerical counts are context for an earlier bounded assessment, **not a publication-qualified model accuracy measurement**. No claim is made about population accuracy, processing completion or Finance automation.

sections.title: Why populated address fields cannot be trusted automatically
sections.markdown:
The handover describes **12 address-designated extraction outputs** that were considered unsupported by the synthetic supplier-invoice source content. The reviewer could not repeat the source-PDF comparison, so those values must remain **reported anomalies**, not independently confirmed current-run failures. No document-linked technical trace is established here.

**Proposed future safeguard, not demonstrated in KS05:** verify extracted fields against source evidence and authorized master data; route unsupported values to human review or a quarantine queue before any Finance posting workflow. This exercise does **not** prove that such a safeguard was implemented, triggered, or enforced.

sections.title: Five distinct architecture boundaries
sections.markdown:
**Proposed controlled processing design; none of these end-to-end controls was qualified by this exercise:**

1. **Extract:** obtain structured header and line-item candidates.
2. **Validate:** check source support, mandatory fields and arithmetic with reproducible evidence.
3. **Resolve identity:** compare supplier and purchasing fields with authorized business records.
4. **Apply enterprise controls:** use the actual target FI/MM or invoice-management environment for configured rules.
5. **Authorize actions:** separate validation and business approval from any posting or payment operation.

The handover reports an extraction comparison, but the later independent review did **not** reproduce it. No current-run evidence was supplied for supplier matching, configured duplicate checking, quarantine, posting or payments.

sections.title: Compared with OCR and other IDP services
sections.markdown:
**Use the tool that best supports a controlled business outcome, not the tool with the strongest AI branding.** No comparative OCR/IDP trial was part of KS05.

| Criterion | Existing OCR / IDP | SAP Document AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recognition | OCR turns scans into text; existing IDP may also classify and extract fields | Document AI can use OCR as part of document processing |
| Invoice field extraction | Text-only OCR needs downstream parsing; mature IDP may already produce structured data | Document AI supports extraction of structured headers and line items with supported methods |
| Enrichment | Depends on existing products and integration | Document AI offers documented enrichment capabilities; does not prove supplier/PO business validation |
| Exceptions / business rules | Must be designed and governed | Still requires source grounding, master data checks, duplicate handling and approval |
| Cost / value | Reuse may avoid an extra platform | Adopt only when independently measured benefit justifies integration and service cost |

**Recommended decision test:** send the same representative invoices through both options, independently score all required fields (including unsupported values), quantify reviewer corrections and exception handling, verify master-data and SAP integration requirements, and compare all-in **cost per accepted invoice**. Neither option is a proven winner here.

Where supplier invoices arrive as structured electronic messages, first determine whether OCR is required at all.

sections.title: What the evidence does not establish
sections.markdown:
**Limits of the reviewed publication evidence:**

- **Source evidence:** the handover-reported PDF/export field reconciliation was **not independently replayed** in the R2 review; direct document-ID linkage is also unverified.
- **Numerical findings:** 34/34 selected matches and 12 questionable address outputs are **reported values**, not independently reproduced findings for this release candidate.
- **Tenant status:** no fresh authenticated full-catalog or current job-status readback was supplied to this review.
- **Business controls:** no trace in the reviewed material proves supplier-master matching, FI/MM duplicate enforcement, source-field quarantine, document posting or payment.
- **Comparative value:** no OCR/IDP benchmark, workload study or cost comparison was supplied.
- **Scope decision:** Finance Phase 2 was **not executed in the documented KS05 scope**. The public evidence does not independently establish a specific cause for that decision.

A missing evidence receipt must not be interpreted as proof that a function failed or that SAP Document AI cannot support it.

sections.title: Decision and learning
sections.markdown:
**Publication decision:** Treat KS05 as a bounded handover-based learning note about the difference between extracted invoice fields and evidence-backed Finance processing. The handover reports 34/34 selected expected matches and 12 address-field concerns, but the independent reviewer did **not** reproduce that reconciliation.

**What this can support:** a concrete discussion of source verification, provenance and control design. **What it cannot support:** qualified model accuracy, a confirmed live status, functioning duplicate prevention, implemented quarantine, AP automation or superiority to another solution.

**Community question:** Before using extracted invoice fields in Finance, which source-to-field and business-control evidence would you demand?
